records.plant_name: Monarch Rock Air data center campus (Rockford)
records.monitor_reason: A gas generation plan for this data center is not confirmed by any source I could read, and no capacity, equipment or permit is public.
records.researcher_notes: Monarch Rock Air, a company tied to Monarch Energy, plans a data center campus on Friday Road in Rockford, Illinois. A Rock River Current article from June 2026, based on state incentive records, says the campus has associated power generation and is a 1,400 megawatt phased data center. That is the size of the data center, not of any power plant. The task list mentions 250 MW of gas engines planned for 2027 from Monarch's own website. I could not confirm that: the Monarch page is built with scripts and showed no text about Illinois or engines, and other articles describe ComEd grid supply. Still unknown: fuel, number of engines, generating capacity and air permit. Check for an Illinois air permit application. If added later, the captive fields are captive industry use power and captive industry type data center.

records.monitor_reason: The source gives a data center size of 50 MW and names no gas generation.
records.researcher_notes: Hut 8 announced four data center sites in Louisiana, Texas and Illinois. A Data Center Dynamics article says the Illinois site, called Project 4, totals 50 MW. The source does not say where in Illinois, and does not say the site will make its own power from gas. The possible-updates sheet row mentions 1.5 GW across Texas and Illinois, but the Illinois share is only 50 MW. Still unknown: town, power source, any gas turbines or engines and their capacity. It stays on the list only to see whether on-site gas is announced. If added later, the captive fields are captive industry use power and captive industry type data center.

records.plant_name: Joliet Technology Center data center campus
records.monitor_reason: The campus is approved at 1.8 GW of data center capacity, but no gas power plant is named.
records.researcher_notes: The Joliet city council approved the PowerHouse Data Centers and Hillwood campus in March 2026. A Data Center Dynamics article says it will offer up to 1.8 GW at full buildout, built in four phases, each with its own six-acre substation. The article describes grid substations and names no on-site gas turbines or engines. Still unknown: whether any on-site gas generation will be built, and its capacity. Only a gas plant tied to this campus would be added. If added later, the captive fields are captive industry use power and captive industry type data center.
